answer: Submissions that land within 241 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The trellis detector writes to walnut, and umber publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole swarm fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 281 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 3 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
